findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` returns false on both branches (lines 196-199). `!IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` is true when the flag is off, so the `if` returns false there. When the flag is on, the function falls through to `return false`. The `sqlExpressions` toggle therefore has no effect, and the name and the `enabled` variable say the opposite of what the code does. The result is the same as the stub `DB`, which returns "not implemented" for every call. A reader will assume the flag still gates the feature. Replace it with an unconditional early return. For example: `return eq, fmt.Errorf("sql expressions are disabled")` with a comment saying the DuckDB-backed implementation was removed. Delete the helper and the unused `features` read in that branch.

findings.title: Stale `duckDB` variable name and dead parsing code
findings.body: The local variable is still named `duckDB`, but go-duck is removed and `NewInMemoryDB()` now returns a stub. `TablesList` now always returns the error from `RunCommands`, so `tablesFromAST` and the AST helpers are unreachable outside tests. Their tests are skipped with `t.Skip()` (`pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go`, `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go`). Rename the variable, and consider a comment saying the code is kept for re-enabling.

contracts.action: SQL expression query (type "sql") parsed through ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery
contracts.equivalent_path: Legacy path: nodes.go UnmarshalSQLCommand -> NewSQLCommand -> sql.TablesList
contracts.before_after: Before, SQL queries were parsed and executed via go-duck. Now the reader path always returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" before reading the query. The legacy path in nodes.go:159-160 has no flag gate. It reaches TablesList, which calls the stub RunCommands. That returns "not implemented", which NewSQLCommand (sql_command.go:30-36) turns into a BadRequest "error reading SQL command". Both entry points therefore reject SQL queries, with different messages.
contracts.visible_effect: Users running SQL expressions get an error (a 400 on the legacy path, a plain error on the reader path). The feature is disabled.
contracts.failure_mode: Fails closed and visibly with an error. If SQL expressions were saved in existing alert rules or dashboards, they will now error on evaluation.

summary: The PR removes go-duck and replaces it with a stub `sql.DB` that returns \"not implemented\". It also makes the reader reject SQL queries unconditionally. Both SQL entry points fail with an error, so the feature is disabled as the title says. The go.mod and go.sum removals match, and no other references to go-duck remain in the repository. The one real issue is `enableSqlExpressions`, which returns false on every path and so makes the `sqlExpressions` flag meaningless. It is misleading but harmless, so I rated it \"consider\". A second, smaller cleanup note covers the stale `duckDB` variable name and the now-unreachable parsing code in `parser.go`.
